blogPosts.title: How Much Does Graphene Floor Coating Cost in Southbank?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the cost of graphene floor coatings in Southbank. From $50/sqm for standard to custom pricing for large areas — get a full breakdown.
body: If you’re a Southbank business owner or homeowner considering protective coatings, the cost is often the first question. Graphene-enhanced floor coatings are a premium product, but they offer long-term savings by reducing maintenance and extending surface life. In this guide, we break down pricing factors specific to the Southbank and Melbourne area.

Standard residential garage or patio coatings typically start around $50 per square metre. This includes surface preparation, one coat of graphene primer and a topcoat. For larger commercial spaces like warehouses or retail floors, pricing can drop to $35–$45 per square metre due to scale, but may require additional prep work. Industrial applications with heavy-duty requirements often range from $60–$80 per square metre.

Several factors influence your final quote: floor condition, size, access limitations and whether you need chemical-resistant or anti-slip finishes. Southbank properties in older buildings may need more extensive concrete repair before coating. Our team always provides a free on-site assessment to give you an accurate fixed price with no surprises.

Graphene coatings outperform traditional epoxy or polyurethane because the nano-particles bind at a molecular level, creating a denser, more flexible film. This means fewer coats are needed, reducing labour costs over time. One graphene coating can last 5–10 years with proper maintenance, compared to 2–3 years for standard coatings.

We also offer optional UV-stable and anti-bacterial formulations for healthcare, childcare and aged care facilities. These add a small premium but improve indoor air quality and comply with strict health regulations. In Southbank’s mixed-use precincts, many property managers choose these upgrades for tenant safety.

Ready for a quote? Contact our Southbank team for a free, no-obligation site inspection. We’ll walk you through the best graphene coating system for your surface and budget. All quotes are fixed and we’ll never upsell unnecessary services.

blogPosts.title: Best Time to Apply Protective Coatings in Melbourne’s Climate
blogPosts.excerpt: Melbourne’s weather can be tricky for coating projects. Learn the ideal conditions for applying graphene coatings in Southbank and how we work around rain and cold.
body: Melbourne is famous for four seasons in one day, and that variability can affect coating applications. For best results, graphene coatings should be applied when the ambient temperature is between 10°C and 35°C, with relative humidity below 85%. In Southbank, the ideal months are typically late spring (October–November) and early autumn (March–April).

During summer, extreme heat can cause coatings to cure too quickly, leading to uneven finish. Winter’s cold and damp can slow curing and risk moisture entrapment. Our team monitors weather forecasts and uses dehumidifiers and heaters for indoor projects if needed. We also schedule outdoor work during stable windows.

For Southbank properties near the Yarra River, morning dew and coastal air can increase humidity. We conduct moisture tests on the substrate before any application. If the concrete or stone is too damp, we delay until surface moisture drops below acceptable levels. This attention to detail ensures a bond that lasts.

Indoor coatings are less weather-dependent, but we still control temperature and ventilation. In commercial kitchens, medical facilities or retail spaces, we often apply coatings after hours or on weekends to minimise disruption. The graphene nano-technology cures to full hardness within 72 hours, though light foot traffic can resume after 24 hours.

One advantage of graphene coatings is their flexibility. They expand and contract with temperature changes better than traditional coatings, reducing cracking in Melbourne’s variable climate. This makes them ideal for exposed concrete slabs and stone floors that experience thermal movement.

If you’re planning a coating project, contact us for a pre-weather assessment. We’ll advise the best window and provide climate-controlled solutions for your Southbank property. No project is too small or too tricky.

blogPosts.title: Graphene vs Epoxy: Which Coating Is Better for Your Southbank Home?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering whether to choose graphene or epoxy for your garage, patio or basement? We compare durability, cost and appearance for Southbank homeowners.
body: Choosing between graphene and epoxy coatings can be confusing. Both protect concrete and stone surfaces, but they work very differently. Epoxy creates a thick plastic-like layer on top of the substrate, while graphene-infused coatings penetrate and bond at a molecular level. For Southbank homes, graphene often wins on durability and longevity.

Epoxy is widely available and cheaper upfront — around $25–$40 per square metre installed. However, it can yellow under UV light, chip or peel if moisture gets underneath. Graphene coatings cost more initially ($50–$80/sqm) but resist UV, chemicals and impact better. They are also thinner, which means they don’t hide imperfections but create a harder surface.

For garages in Southbank where cars drip oil and brake fluid, graphene’s chemical resistance is a major advantage. Epoxy stains easily from hot tyre marks, whereas graphene can withstand temperatures up to 180°C. For patios exposed to Melbourne’s sun, graphene won’t yellow, keeping the colour vibrant for years.

Appearance-wise, epoxy gives a glossy, thick finish that can look like a wet floor. Graphene offers a more natural, matte or satin sheen that enhances the concrete or stone texture. Many homeowners prefer the subtle look, especially for natural stone surfaces.

Installation time differs too. Epoxy requires multiple thick coats and longer drying times between each. Graphene can be applied in fewer, thinner coats, with full cure in 3 days. Our Southbank team can complete a standard garage in two days, minimising disruption.

Ultimately, if you want a budget-friendly short-term fix, epoxy works. But for a long-lasting, environment-resistant coating that adds value to your Southbank home, graphene is the smarter investment. Contact us for a free consultation and side-by-side sample.

blogPosts.title: How to Maintain Natural Stone Benchtops in Southbank
blogPosts.excerpt: Southbank’s humidity and daily use can take a toll on marble and granite benchtops. Learn the best cleaning and coating practices to keep them pristine.
body: Natural stone benchtops are a beautiful feature in many Southbank apartments and homes, but they require proper care. Marble and granite are porous and can absorb liquids, leading to stains and etching from acidic foods. The good news is that a graphene-based sealer can protect your stone for years without altering its appearance.

We recommend sealing natural stone benchtops every 1–2 years, but our graphene coating lasts up to 15 years. It bonds at the molecular level, filling microscopic pores without forming a film. This prevents water, wine, oil and citrus from penetrating while allowing the stone to breathe. Maintenance becomes as simple as wiping with mild soap and water.

Avoid harsh cleaners containing bleach, ammonia or vinegar — they can damage the sealant over time. Instead, use pH-neutral stone cleaners. For daily cleaning, a soft cloth and warm water are sufficient. Our coating also resists bacterial growth, which is a bonus for kitchen surfaces.

In Southbank’s humid environment, mould and mildew can grow in unsealed stone grout lines. Our graphene sealer is anti-microbial and prevents mould from taking hold. We often apply it to stone splashbacks and bathroom vanities as well as benchtops.

If your existing stone is already stained or etched, our surface preparation service can restore it. We use diamond abrasives and polishing pads to remove minor damage before applying the graphene coating. The result is a like-new surface with enhanced protection.
Protect your investment — contact Pro Image Coating Systems for a free assessment of your Southbank stone surfaces. We’ll quote you for sealing and ongoing care advice. Your benchtops will thank you.
